title: The Whispering Canopy: A Shell Spin into the Golden Slopes
subtitle: In Which Waluigi Screens the Manor Tape and Reviews the Amenities
filed: 1 Aethel 1040 BF — recorded at the projector
pullQuote: A vacation plan with a captive, a damp carpet, and a portal deserves a VERY loud review.
standfirst: Waluigi runs the manor footage through a projector and talks over every gloomy doorway, bad booking choice, and suspicious swirl of green. The tape plays in order; Waluigi can stop it for a heckle, but he cannot skip ahead to the room service.

sections.heading: THE LOBBY IS DARK AND THE PRICE IS UNKNOWN
sections.body:
Waluigi starts the projector on a manor shaped like a jagged shadow, all heavy stone, cracked cobbles, and one flickering lantern doing the work of an entire cheerful neighborhood. The oak doors groan when Archie pushes them open. Waluigi leans toward the screen: the building has not offered a welcome, only a noise that sounds like the hinges are filing a complaint.

Archie looks around the opulent, gloomy foyer and asks, "I wonder how much they charge," which is the first sensible question on this tape and also the first sign that he may be about to pay for a terrible idea. Waluigi points at the shadows: there is no visible price board, just enough atmosphere to make a coin purse sweat.

Remi studies the high ceiling and says, "Even with the light in here it's pretty dark," a sentence that should make the projector bulb file for hazard pay. Green T surveys the same entrance and asks, "Is this the best idea?" Waluigi gives the screen a sharp pause. THAT is the correct question, delivered before the group has even learned the rate.

But Remi is already more curious than afraid. She decides, "Well, it's kinda interesting in here we should stay." Waluigi resumes the tape with the expression of a commentator watching somebody choose the suspicious door because the wallpaper is intriguing. Archie tightens his pack strap under the weight of the atmosphere, and the group moves deeper into the foyer. The cost is still unknown; the curiosity bill is now OPEN. Waluigi calls it a VERY DARK, LOW-BUDGET WELCOME: one lantern, deep shadows, and STILL no price in sight. WAH!

sections.heading: THE CAPTIVE IS NOT BUYING THE FRIENDSHIP PITCH
sections.body:
The manor swallows the group's voices, and Waluigi turns up the projector volume as Rivers strains against his bonds. His fury is plain; Markup remains stiff and unmoved. Markup says, "Sorry, you're coming with us," with all the warmth of a locked door. Waluigi swivels toward the audience: this is not the moment to call a captive luggage unless the luggage has just asked to be released.

Remi answers the tension with a song, apparently treating the rafters as her personal stage. She sings, "You are our toads within our chains from where your from to where we are," then continues, "Oh, I'm a new toad, listen to me, I'll sing you a song of the air and the sea," while Rivers is still bound and angry. Waluigi freezes the frame on that contrast: one person is protesting, one person is singing, and the room has somehow become a very gloomy talent show.

Archie watches Remi, then turns his attention back to Rivers. He tries, "Maybe we can be friends after we stay at the inn," and follows with, "Why do you hate him?" Waluigi puts both hands up at the screen. The answer is not hidden in the manor's architecture; the captive gives it immediately: "Because you kidnapped me!"

That lands with less mystery than the stone walls and more force than Remi's chorus. Waluigi can hear the whole friendship pitch wobble under one plainly stated fact. Rivers is being taken along, Markup is not softening, and Remi's song has not changed the situation. The group continues toward reception with the tension still wound tight. Waluigi lets the tape roll, because the next stop is apparently where they plan to ask the building for a room while bringing an unwilling guest. Waluigi labels the exchange NO CONSENT, BAD TIMING, and a FRIENDSHIP PITCH that needs work; the prisoner answers plainly. WAH, what a check-in.

sections.heading: THE FOUNDER, THE WET FLOOR, AND THE WAITING PATRON
sections.body:
The footage opens on dust, old velvet, carved ceilings, and Remi peeling away from the group toward a tall stone-and-marble statue. Waluigi taps the projector frame: the statue has a name, and Remi supplies it at once: "Wow, who's this? Our founder, Alda Farum. Thanks for the information!" The delivery is so brisk that Waluigi barely has time to admire the frozen founder before Remi is moving again.

Her foot finds moisture, her balance goes, and she slides across the floor. Waluigi makes a little rewind gesture; the wet patch has won this round without so much as a speech. Remi spots a nearby Goomba and greets it, then turns to a tired traveler waiting with a partner for a room. The traveler says, "A long time... like an eternity," which Waluigi considers an alarming review from someone still sitting in the lobby.

Remi asks about the looming figure. The patron explains, "He throws the meanest greenest hammers; if you ask him, he can do it." Waluigi looks at Green T, then back at the projector: the conversation has moved from room delays to hammer credentials in record time. Remi answers, "I don't want to break anything," while Archie says they are there to relax and get their bearings. Waluigi circles RELAX in the air with a very imaginary marker.

Remi notices the lower hallway; Archie says nothing much is happening there, just a hallway. She is wet from the floor and warns, "Be careful, this carpet was just mopped. Look how wet I am," before Archie keeps her from running off. He tells Rivers to stay with them until they have questions, adding that he is neutral while Markup wants him. Waluigi watches the party gather itself and head toward reception: the statue is behind them, the carpet is still damp, and nobody has found a peaceful corner yet. Waluigi names this sequence STATUE, SLIP, GOOMBA, WAITING ROOM, HAMMER TALK: the lobby is giving out side quests before check-in. WAH!

sections.heading: ROOM OPTIONS, COINS, AND A SEARCH AT THE DESK
sections.body:
At reception, the Magikoopa attendant leans over a polished stone counter and asks, "Can I see your reservation?" Waluigi pauses the projector on Archie's face as he reaches into his pouch and produces money instead. Archie says, "I only have money," which is not the password the attendant requested, but it is at least an honest description of the contents. The screen has not supplied a booking confirmation.

The attendant looks over the group and directs, "Check her boys. Koopas surround her." Several guards step forward and search the travelers for hidden weapons. Waluigi's eyebrows climb past the frame: a room inquiry has turned into a security search before anybody has even chosen the wallpaper. He does not add a single fact to the picture; the shells gleam, claws click, and the search proceeds methodically.

Then the Magikoopa slides over a tablet of unusual accommodations, each with an illustration and a warning. Waluigi asks the audience to keep their eyes on the options: the Whispering Canopy, the Bleeding Chandelier Suite, the Forgotten Ballroom Chamber, the Root-Cellar Crypt, and the Mirror That Watches Back. This is a menu that has apparently confused lodging with a dare.

Archie studies the prices and descriptions, weighing cost against the strange choices, while Remi looks ready to object to anything without enough flair. Waluigi leans into the projector beam and announces that the hotel has offered five ways to sleep badly, but the tape has not yet told him which one wins. The search has left its own tension in the room; the group stands at the threshold of the manor's private spaces, and Archie's money is still the only reservation-shaped object anyone has produced. Waluigi calls these FIVE HAUNTED ROOM OPTIONS IN HOTEL CLOTHING; every title sounds like a dare in decorative lettering. Waluigi releases the pause. NEXT, the group has to pick a room.

sections.heading: THE CHEAPER ROOM GETS A VERY ENTHUSIASTIC VOTE
sections.body:
The screen returns to the open register and the prices. Archie admits, "I compromise because it's cheaper and I don't want Remi to throw a fit," which Waluigi hears as a budget decision carrying a second, much louder passenger. Remi leans over him and makes her choice clear: "I want to go to the Whispering Canopy!" Waluigi points to the name as it appears on the tablet. It is not a sunny meadow; the room name itself whispers that the night's going to be strange.

A formally dressed Koopa appears from the hallway with a clipboard and asks, "Reservation?" Archie answers, "I don't have that, I only have money." Waluigi stops the tape again. The party has a selected room, a pile of coins, and no reservation; the conversation is doing laps around the same missing piece. The Koopa does not make a speech about it. The group goes toward the assigned chamber.

Thick grey carpet muffles their steps. At the threshold stands a shimmering archway, humming with a vibration strong enough to make their teeth ache. The Koopa announces, "The Whispering Canopy is prepared," and remains blank-faced. Waluigi points at that contrast: the gateway is making a noise in their teeth, while the attendant presents the emotional range of a wall.

Archie grips Remi's hand so she stays close as they enter the small transition space. The air carries crushed herbs and wet earth; the Koopa stands by the controls with a hand hovering near them. Waluigi narrates the frame without skipping: they have not stepped into a normal bedroom, only up to the teleporter. The choice is made, the portal is ready, and the next detail is still on the other side. Waluigi awards the archway ZERO STARS for COMFORT and FIVE STARS for making everyone's teeth hurt before arrival. WAH, the amenities are getting WEIRDER.

sections.heading: THE ROOM IS A LONG WAY FROM THE INN
sections.body:
The transition room smells of old parchment and ozone, with damp carpet clinging to the travelers' boots. A teleporter stands in the middle, framed in dark polished wood. Waluigi lets the projector linger on it: this is no ordinary bed-and-breakfast doorway, and the machine has become the central furnishing. Green T steps forward and insists, "We paid for this and I am not letting money OR room service go to waste!" He enters the swirling light. Waluigi gives the screen a decisive point at OR: the capital letters are doing a lot of work.

The portal flashes white and swallows Green T. A Koopa in a crisp suit stays by the controls, then explains, "The teleporter brings them to the Golden Slopes, a specialized room far away," and adds, "Simply leave the room and exit in the slope or ring the bell," Waluigi repeats those directions in a grand hotel voice, then drops it. The room is far away, and the way out is a slope or a bell. No elevator pitch could make that sound ordinary.

Archie looks between the portal and the group, feeling the size of what the inn has connected. Waluigi watches his realization land: the manor is a facade for a wider network of remote rooms, not just one spooky building with a hallway. The group stands in heavy silence as the distance sinks in. The tape does not say that everyone has been scattered; it says the room is remote and the travelers are no longer in the manor's heart. Waluigi keeps the wording careful, even while the projector throws a very dramatic WHITE glow across the wall.

The accommodation has transported them to the Golden Slopes, and the Koopa has explained how to leave or call. Waluigi is still on the same frame, not pretending the portal has solved the larger mystery. Green T has refused to waste the purchase, the others are faced with a distant room, and the next recorded beat takes the group back outside. Waluigi hears FAR AWAY, SPECIALIZED ROOM, EXIT IN THE SLOPE, RING THE BELL and asks where the ordinary bed went. WAH, what a vacation package.

sections.heading: RIVERS BLAMES SPEAKER L AND PRAISES HIMSELF
sections.body:
The projector shows the group beyond the hotel threshold, with the door thudding shut behind them and a green haze lying over the town. Archie scans vacant streets and senses a rhythmic pulse of mana. He says, "This is the first time I’ve encountered this," then immediately adds, "But we have more pressing things." Waluigi raises one finger toward the screen: Archie has noticed something new and has chosen to continue with the urgent matter in hand. The tape does not tell Waluigi what the haze means yet.

Archie brings Rivers into the clearing and asks, "Alright, Rivers... what happened to the toads?" Rivers names Speaker L: "Speaker L led them astray. He betrayed them. He led them into a death manor." Waluigi freezes on the word betrayed. This is Rivers's account, not a neutral tour guide, and the projector keeps his accusation in the center of the frame.

Archie asks, "You really don't like Speaker L, do you?" Rivers answers, "I don't like him because he was ignorant!" He says Speaker L did not know how to wield his power or understand how strong Rivers was. Archie calls Speaker L a tyrant and says that is understandable. Waluigi turns to the audience: the conversation is moving from what happened to why Rivers believes he should have been in charge.

Rivers says he is different because he is stronger than the other toads, whom he calls weaklings, and says they need a leader like him. Waluigi taps the screen as Rivers's self-description grows larger than the green haze behind him. No one has yet confirmed every part of his accusation; the footage gives us the words he chooses and Archie's questions. Waluigi keeps the tape rolling, because the street is empty, the mana pulse remains, and Rivers has just made his claim about leadership. Waluigi's projector shows ONE ACCUSATION, TWO QUESTIONS, and a very large claim about who deserves to lead. WAH, that is quite a speech for someone still being questioned.

sections.heading: ARCHIE CALLS THE STRANGE ATMOSPHERE USUAL
sections.body:
The town is a hollow, silent shell, with green haze clinging to cobblestones and storefronts. Archie steps through it, listening to the stillness and feeling the copper-and-moss air. He says, "Seems usual. Let's head back to the cliff," but the narration notes that his voice lacks its usual certainty. Waluigi stops the projector on the contradiction: the town looks wrong, the sound is absent, and the line says usual. That is a VERY interesting use of the word.

Archie senses a thrumming vibration and recognizes the signature of a ritual nearby. He pauses, looks over the empty streets, and says, "This is the first time I encountered this but we have more pressing things." Waluigi lets the silence sit for a moment. The ritual is not merely a spooky color effect in the description; Archie identifies a magical expenditure, and the haze continues to pulse as he weighs what to do.

Here Waluigi drops the showman's voice for four short sentences. The green mist is present in the scene, and the account says Archie feels the ritual's pulse. The streets are empty in the image the story gives us. Waluigi grants those physical details plainly; they are not a projector trick.

Then the performance snaps back on. Archie says, "Alright, excellent! Let's do it here since no one is here," and moves farther into the haze rather than returning to the cliff. Waluigi throws both arms toward the screen: the decision has arrived while the ritual remains nearby and the town remains abandoned. He does not pretend to know what is around the next turn. The group goes forward with purpose, leaving the outskirts behind. Waluigi gives the audience one last look at the empty storefronts, then lets the tape run. Waluigi circles EMPTY STREETS, GREEN HAZE, RITUAL PULSE: Archie has noticed every warning sign and advances anyway. WAH! The scene is not getting LESS suspicious.

sections.heading: A STAFF IS HELD OUT FOR A CLOSER LOOK
sections.body:
The next hallway beat begins after the mana regulators have been deactivated and the cultists' retreat has left echoes behind. Dust hangs in the still air. Archie turns toward Remi and asks, "Can I see that staff a bit? You don't have to give it to me you can hold it out in front of me," Waluigi pauses the picture on the wording: this is a request to inspect, with the staff still in Remi's hands. Archie is careful to say she need not give it over.

Remi hesitates, tightens her fingers around the wood, then relaxes. She replies, "Okay, I see no consequences to these actions," and extends the artifacts slowly. Waluigi stares at the sentence, then at the objects moving across the gap. The timing is COMEDY, but the account still tells us she offers them deliberately and the air hums with a faint static charge.

Archie steps close and says, "Here, have a look," as the staff comes inches from his vision. The story says it is directly in his face; he studies its carvings and feels energy from the wood. Waluigi leans away from the projector as if distance might help. The joke writes itself without adding an explosion, a spell, or any other event the tape does not show.

For a heartbeat, the exchange is a temporary truce of trust in a place that has felt predatory. Waluigi lowers his voice just enough to let that fact land, then raises it again: the artifacts are being handled carefully, but the surroundings still do not feel safe. Distant rhythmic footsteps approach from the main hall. Waluigi points at the sound—INSPECTION TIME IS OVER. The group has had a moment with the staff, and now the pressure of the unknown is pressing back in from every side. Waluigi labels the moment CAREFUL HANDOFF, FACE-LEVEL STAFF, and FOOTSTEPS APPROACHING; the hallway is not finished interrupting them. WAH, move along!

sections.heading: THE SHELL SPINS AND THE GROUP TAKES THE PORTAL
sections.body:
The chamber door groans under a sudden impact; dust dances as the air pressure shifts. A suited Koopa bursts through and shouts, "He's coming through!" Waluigi jumps up beside the projector: the warning is real, the door is swinging, and the picture has not yet explained who is coming. He refuses to skip ahead.

A large shell spins in the center of the room, carving a circle through the air. Remi lunges, grabs it, and launches herself into the shimmering rift, crying, "Weeeeee!" Waluigi grabs the frame as she vanishes into the light. Archie recoils; the shell's momentum threatens to knock him flat. That is a lot of motion for a room whose reservation conversation was about a canopy.

Archie takes a breath and says, "You know what, no I'm being a wuss," before deciding, "Let's go in the teleporter." Waluigi rewinds half a second to let the self-description play again, then points at the portal: Archie is opting for the hotel's remote accommodation rather than the shell's spinning route. The group retreats toward the teleporter and the Golden Slopes, leaving the Koopa behind as the shell's echoes fade.

The film does show that the shell spins hard enough for Archie to recoil. Remi does disappear into the rift; that is not a gentle step through a doorway. Waluigi concedes those physical facts without a joke for a brief moment. The momentum is real, and Archie has reason to choose another route.

Then Waluigi is back on his feet, shouting over the projector fan. The room remains unsettled by the warning about someone coming through, and the record ends this immediate journey with the group heading into the teleporter. Waluigi does not invent the identity of the approaching figure or a result beyond the account. The last frame is the retreat, the fading spin, and a manor whose secrets are not settled. Waluigi freezes on SPINNING SHELL, OPEN DOOR, and TELEPORTER RETREAT; the tape ends with urgency, not an answer. WAH! Roll the credits—carefully.
